hyperedges.label: Fairness computation pipeline (verified tasks + reviews to report)

nodes.label: FairShare
nodes.rationale: Web app that makes group grades match who actually did the work, by making effort visible rather than punishing anyone.

nodes.label: Social Loafing
nodes.rationale: People exert less effort in a group than alone. This is the core problem FairShare exists to counter; documented by Latane, Williams & Harkins (1979).

nodes.label: Ringelmann Effect
nodes.rationale: Older finding that per-person effort drops as group size grows; the basis social loafing builds on.

nodes.label: Peer Assessment
nodes.rationale: Teammates rating each other is shown to be fair and accurate vs teacher marks (Falchikov & Goldfinch 2000). Justifies FairShare's private peer-review mechanism.

nodes.label: CATME
nodes.rationale: Existing college peer-evaluation tool; FairShare adapts the same idea to be free and student-run with no teacher account.

nodes.label: FairShare (App)
nodes.rationale: Web app that makes school group projects fair by tracking who actually does the work: teammates join with a code, work off a live task board, completed work needs a proof link plus a teammate's verification, and at the end everyone privately rates each other. Produces a printable fairness report for the teacher. Built by a high-school student for the Congressional App Challenge.

nodes.label: Tech Stack (Vite + React + plain JS + Firebase Spark)
nodes.rationale: Vite + React + plain JavaScript (no TypeScript) + Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Hosting), free Spark tier only, no Cloud Functions. Chosen because developer knows JS/HTML/CSS but is new to React/Firebase; free tier constrains all logic to the client. Allowed deps only: react, react-dom, react-router-dom, firebase. No UI kits, no Tailwind; hand-written CSS with design tokens.
nodes.norm_label: tech stack (vite + react + plain js + firebase spark)

nodes.label: No Cloud Functions constraint
nodes.rationale: Spark (free) tier only means no server code; all logic is client-side and security is enforced solely by Firestore rules. This forces the report math to run in the browser, which is why review docs become readable to members after project end.

nodes.label: Google Sign-in (Auth)
nodes.rationale: Google sign-in only (popup). useAuth hook + auth context handle sign-in/out, loading state; protected routes redirect to landing. Web API keys are safe to commit.

nodes.label: Firestore Data Model
nodes.rationale: Root collections projects and joinCodes; subcollections tasks and reviews under each project. memberIds array kept for security rules + queries; members map kept for display. joinCodes/{CODE} exists as a lookup so non-members can find a project to join.

nodes.label: projects collection
nodes.rationale: projects/{projectId} with name, createdBy, createdAt, status (active|ended), endedAt, joinCode, memberIds array, members map. Read only by members; only the creator can set status ended.

nodes.label: joinCodes collection
nodes.rationale: joinCodes/{CODE} maps a 6-char code to a projectId so a non-member can look up and join. Readable by any signed-in user; created only alongside the project by its creator.

nodes.label: tasks subcollection
nodes.rationale: projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId} with title, size (S|M|L = 1/2/3 points), status (todo|doing|done|verified), assignee (uid|null; null = claimable), proofUrl (required to enter done), verifiedBy/verifiedAt, lastRejection. Read/write members only; verification writes require verifiedBy == auth.uid != assignee.

nodes.label: reviews subcollection
nodes.rationale: projects/{projectId}/reviews/{reviewerUid}, one doc per reviewer, holding a ratings map keyed by revieweeUid with effort/quality/teamwork (1-5) + comment. Own doc always readable/writable; others' review docs readable only when parent project status == ended, so the client can compute report math without Cloud Functions. Known tradeoff: a determined member could read raw ratings via devtools after end; UI only shows averages and anonymized comments.

nodes.label: Join Code (6-char)
nodes.rationale: 6 chars from A-Z + 2-9 (no confusable chars), generated in src/lib/joinCode.js. Teammates join a project by entering the code.

nodes.label: Live Task Board
nodes.rationale: Three columns (To Do / Doing / Done). Tasks can be created unassigned (anyone claims) or assigned to a member. Real-time first: all project/task/review reads use onSnapshot listeners so two browsers stay in sync — the M1 demo wow moment.

nodes.label: Proof + Verification
nodes.rationale: Marking a task done requires a proof URL. Any teammate except the task's assignee can Approve or Reject with a written reason (reject sends the task back to Doing). Verifier identity is stored and shown on the report. Rules enforce verifier != assignee, blocking self-verification.

nodes.label: Peer Review
nodes.rationale: After a project ends, each member privately rates each teammate (not self) 1-5 stars on Effort, Quality, Teamwork, plus an optional comment. One submission per user (doc id = uid). Private.

nodes.label: End Project
nodes.rationale: Only the creator can end a project. Sets status ended + endedAt; board locks read-only and the peer-review phase opens. Rules allow only the creator to set status ended.

nodes.label: Fairness Report
nodes.rationale: Printable web page (browser Print / Save as PDF). Two headline numbers per person — % of verified task points and average peer rating — with NO single combined score, deliberately keeping the two dimensions separate. Generates regardless of missing reviews and lists who didn't submit; averages use whatever exists.

nodes.label: src/lib/fairness.js (pure functions)
nodes.rationale: The fairness math lives in pure functions with zero Firebase imports so the student can read, explain, and unit-test it in isolation. This is the code the user must deeply understand for the judges.

nodes.label: taskPoints(size)
nodes.rationale: Maps size to points: S:1, M:2, L:3. A constant in lib/fairness.js.

nodes.label: contributionShares(tasks, memberIds)
nodes.rationale: For each member: sum of points of their verified tasks divided by total verified points across the project, as a percentage. Also returns raw counts (verified tasks, points). Only verified work counts.

nodes.label: ratingAverages(reviews, memberIds)
nodes.rationale: Per member, per criterion mean of all ratings about them (self-rating not collected), plus overall mean of the three criteria, plus a list of members who never submitted a review.

nodes.label: Firestore Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Since there is no server code, all access control is enforced by Firestore rules. Rules are updated in the same feature that introduces the data they protect, never left for later. Covers member-only project reads, creator-only end, self-add join, verifier != assignee, and post-end review visibility.

nodes.label: One-feature-per-session Workflow
nodes.rationale: Build exactly one feature per session in order; do not scaffold ahead. After each feature: stop, explain in plain English what was built, give a manual two-account test script, and list Firebase Console steps for the user. Ensures a high-school student can explain the app to judges and keeps scope disciplined.

nodes.label: Milestone M1 (live board)
nodes.rationale: 'Two accounts see the same live board' (~Sept 18). Covers F0-F5: scaffold, auth, create/dashboard, join, task board, claim/move.

nodes.label: Milestone M2 (proof/verify/reviews)
nodes.rationale: 'Proof, verification, and peer reviews work' (~Oct 9). Covers F6-F9: mark done with proof, verification, end project, peer review form.

nodes.label: Milestone M3 (report/polish/ship)
nodes.rationale: 'Report, polish, ship' (~Oct 26). Covers F10-F14: fairness math, report page, security audit, visual polish, deploy + demo prep.

nodes.label: F0 Scaffold & design system (done)
nodes.rationale: Done 2026-09-03. Vite React app, folder structure, react-router-dom route map with placeholders, playful design tokens in src/styles/tokens.css, landing page.

nodes.label: F1 Firebase setup + Google sign-in (done)
nodes.rationale: Done 2026-09-10. Firebase Console setup, config in src/lib/firebase.js, useAuth hook + auth context, protected routes, header with user photo/name/sign-out.

nodes.label: F2 Create project + dashboard (done)
nodes.rationale: Done 2026-09-16. Dashboard onSnapshot query on memberIds array-contains uid; create-project modal writes projects doc + joinCodes doc; joinCode generated in src/lib/joinCode.js; first Firestore rules deploy.

nodes.label: F3 Join by code (done)
nodes.rationale: Done 2026-09-16. Look up joinCodes/{CODE}, self-add to memberIds + members (rules permit self-add only), friendly errors, members list with creator badge.

nodes.label: F4 Task board — create & display
nodes.rationale: Three columns with empty states, add-task modal (title, S/M/L size chips, optional assignee), tasks render via onSnapshot on the tasks subcollection. Task rules added.

nodes.label: F5 Claim & move tasks
nodes.rationale: Claim unclaimed tasks (set assignee to self, move to Doing), Start assigned tasks, Mark done stub. Only assignee moves their task; creator can reassign or delete.

nodes.label: F6 Mark done with proof
nodes.rationale: Mark-done modal requires a validated proof URL; task moves to Done styled as waiting-for-verification with a clickable proof link.

nodes.label: F7 Verification — approve or reject
nodes.rationale: Non-assignee members Approve (status verified, store verifiedBy/verifiedAt) or Reject with reason (back to doing, store lastRejection). Rules enforce verifier != assignee.

nodes.label: F8 End project
nodes.rationale: Creator-only End project button sets status ended + endedAt, locks the board read-only, shows a review banner. Rules: only creator can set ended.

nodes.label: F9 Peer review form
nodes.rationale: /project/:id/review (ended only): 1-5 star inputs per teammate for Effort/Quality/Teamwork + comment; one submission per user (doc id = uid). Review rules added (own-doc write, others readable only when ended).

nodes.label: F10 Fairness math (pure functions)
nodes.rationale: Implements taskPoints, contributionShares, ratingAverages in src/lib/fairness.js, written WITH the user and verified against hand-worked examples.

nodes.label: F11 Fairness report page
nodes.rationale: /project/:id/report (ended, members only): headline stat cards, verified-task table with proof links and verifiers, per-criterion averages, anonymized comments, missing-review callout, @media print stylesheet.

nodes.label: F12 Security rules audit + edge cases
nodes.rationale: Full review of firestore.rules against every feature via emulator or second-account probing; adversarial checklist for the user.
nodes.norm_label: f12 security rules audit + edge cases

nodes.label: F13 Visual polish + responsive pass
nodes.rationale: Consistent tokens, designed hover/focus/active states, empty states, compositor-friendly micro-motion respecting prefers-reduced-motion, responsive at 320/768/1024/1440, contrast check. No new features.

nodes.label: F14 Deploy + demo prep
nodes.rationale: firebase init hosting + deploy, add live URL to authorized domains, production smoke test, produce DEMO_SCRIPT.md connecting features to social-loafing research.

nodes.label: Playful & student-y visual style
nodes.rationale: Bright colors, rounded shapes, friendly typography, fun empty states — deliberately must NOT look like a default template. Tokens defined in src/styles/tokens.css (oklch palette, 12-20px radii, rounded display + clean body font pairing, spacing and motion scales).

nodes.label: Real-time onSnapshot listeners
nodes.rationale: All project/task/review reads use onSnapshot listeners rather than one-time gets so two browsers always stay in sync — this live sync is the M1 demo and why every feature gate is a two-account manual test.
